conviction_note: The four filed items are small proxies that roughly offset: a peer galvanizer's strong Jun-Aug coatings quarter and VMI's own beat-and-raise record against steel and diesel costs rising after the July 17 guide assumptions. p_up stays at 50 and abs_move_pct is 6.5, close to the 6.63% event-implied move and the 6.53% median past reaction. The findings sum to -0.2 and the scaled number is 0; the gap is only rounding on balanced evidence.
bar: Q3 2026 EPS about $5.72 on revenue of about $1.11-1.12B. Earnings Whispers gives $5.71 EPS, a $5.81 whisper and $1.12B revenue (https://www.earningswhispers.com/stocks/vmi). Benzinga gives $5.74 EPS and $1.11B (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/VMI/earnings-forecasts, via search snippet). Two sources agree within $0.03. The company guides FY2026 EPS to $22.25-23.50 and net sales to $4.3-4.45B, both raised on 2026-07-21 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000102729/000110465926085223/vmi-20260721xex99d1.htm). H1 EPS was $5.51 + $6.14 = $11.65, so the guide implies H2 EPS of $10.60-11.85 (midpoint $11.23). Consensus Q3 $5.72 plus Zacks Q4 $5.59 is $11.31, and FY consensus is about $22.96 against a $22.875 guide midpoint (https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/zacks-research-has-strong-estimate-for-vmi-fy2026-earnings-2026-08-04/). The bar therefore sits slightly above the guide midpoint and already assumes a small beat or raise. The print_vs_bar estimate of +3% rests on the last two quarters' beats of about 6-7% ($6.14 vs ~$5.75-5.80), reduced for Q3 cost inflation.
positioning_check: Short interest is 417,622 shares, 2.19% of float, with 2.0 days to cover as of the 2026-09-30 report (FINRA, published 2026-10-09; https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NYSE/VMI/short-interest). That is not a crowded short. The 25-delta skew is +1.81 vol points (mild put premium) and the baseline's priced_direction_lean is 'balanced'. Put/call open-interest ratio is 1.96, but total open interest is only 77 contracts and the ATM spread is 24% of mid, so the chain is thin. The 6.63% event-implied move is broadly consistent with Earnings Whispers' ±8.44% and the 6.53% median past reaction. The tape is soft: -4.15% over 5 days, -4.57% over 20 days, 23% below the 52-week high, and about 12% below the $506 open of the Q2 print week. No company-specific cause for the slide was found.

findings.finding: AZZ, the largest US hot-dip galvanizer and a direct peer of VMI's North America Coatings line, reported on 2026-10-13 for its quarter ended 2026-08-31, which overlaps two-thirds of VMI's Q3 (Jun 28 - Sep 26). Metal Coatings sales rose 22.9% to $233.5M at a 30.7% EBITDA margin, on higher steel volume from construction, industrial, infrastructure and transportation markets plus higher prices, and AZZ raised FY guidance. VMI's NA Coatings grew 16.6% in Q2. This points to coatings staying strong in Q3, but coatings is under ~10% of VMI sales, and one analyst on AZZ's call flagged zinc inflation for the next quarter.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Coatings has never been the line VMI traded on. The last prints moved on Utility (+11.9% on 2026-04-21, when NA Utility grew +27%) and on Ag/Telecom softness (-3.9% on 2026-07-21 despite a beat and raise).
findings.why_not_priced: AZZ reported after VMI last spoke and after VMI's Q3 estimates were last revised (Zacks, early August). VMI fell about 4% in the five sessions after AZZ's release, so the tape shows no read-through being bought. It is a peer read on a small segment, so the price would barely move on it even if fully absorbed.
findings.independence: Single document: AZZ's own release. The analyst zinc caveat comes from AZZ call coverage (https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/transcript-what-azz-azz-said-on-its-q2-earnings-call-2026-10-14/). Nothing VMI-specific confirms it.

findings.finding: US hot-rolled coil kept rising after VMI set its guide on steel futures as of 2026-07-17. Nucor's spot price was $1,130-1,145/short ton through July with the SMU average at about $1,165 on July 21; by September 28 Nucor's CSP was $1,220 after weekly $10 raises, and the SMU average neared $1,300 on September 22. That is roughly 5-10% more inflation than at the guide date. On the Q2 call the CFO said steel was already up 27-30% year to date, that material inflation would pressure margins in Q3 as well, and that utility pricing offsets it with a lag. This puts the Infrastructure margin and the Q4 cost commentary at modest risk.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: On 2026-07-21 the CFO flagged material-cost pressure on Infrastructure margins while EPS beat and the guide was raised, and the stock fell 3.9%. That is consistent with cost commentary weighing, but the Ag and Telecom softness reported the same day confounds it.
findings.why_not_priced: Part of this is inside the guide: management said Q3 margins would be pressured and the futures curve on July 17 may already have priced some of the rise. Only the increment above July futures is new. If the market had priced a margin cut, consensus would have come down since August; it has not (the Q3 EPS bar is $5.71-5.74, FY about $22.96, above the guide midpoint).
findings.independence: July levels come from Steel Market Update (https://www.steelmarketupdate.com/2026/07/20/nucor-holds-spot-hr-price-at-1135-ton/), a different source from the GMK/Kallanish September figures. Management's own statement on Q3 margin pressure is in the Q2 call summary (https://www.marketbeat.com/earnings/reports/2026-7-21-valmont-industries-inc-stock/). This is a commodity proxy; VMI also holds HRC hedges, so transmission to its P&L is unconfirmed.

findings.finding: Diesel hit record highs in early September 2026, nearly double its pre-war level, after Houthi/Ansar Allah attacks on Saudi energy facilities lifted Brent back toward $99 from about $90 in August. The Strait of Hormuz has been mostly shut since the US-Israel war with Iran began in late February. On the Q2 call VMI cited diesel up 45% year to date as a cost, guided to 'minimal projects' in the Middle East, and its FY guide assumed conditions as of July 17. This means more freight-cost pressure and weaker irrigation economics than the guide assumed.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: International Ag fell 28.9% in Q2 on the Middle East conflict and the stock fell 3.9% on that print, with Ag softness cited as one reason (https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/valmont-industries-nysevmi-lowered-to-hold-rating-by-zacks-research-2026-07-22/).
findings.why_not_priced: The macro move is public, but its effect on VMI's cost line and Middle East projects has not been confirmed by the company or a counterparty since July. Ag sales guidance ($0.9-0.95B) was left unchanged in July, so a cut would be news. The Middle East shortfall itself was already guided, which limits the size.
findings.independence: US pump-price coverage from mid-September (https://okcfox.com/news/nation-world/gallery/houthi-escalation-in-the-middle-east-brings-new-pain-at-the-pump-for-americans-energy-war-gas-prices?photo=1) points the same way, but it is a photo caption. This is a macro-to-company proxy with no VMI confirmation.

findings.finding: VMI has beaten and raised in both 2026 quarters. Q1 EPS was $5.51 (+27.5%) and the EPS guide went to $21.50-23.50; Q2 EPS was $6.14 against ~$5.75-5.80 consensus and the guide went to $22.25-23.50, with Infrastructure sales guidance raised to $3.4-3.5B. On the Q2 call management said Utility demand was 'robust and strong', growth was constrained by capacity rather than demand, back-half Infrastructure margins would be consistent with the first half, and capex would be weighted to H2 for utility capacity. A third beat and a guide narrowing upward is the base case, but the market's bar already sits above the guide midpoint, and the Q2 beat and raise was sold 3.9%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guidance raises have been met both ways. 2026-04-21: EPS guide raised, +11.93%. 2026-07-21: beat and raise, -3.9%. 2026-02-17 (FY26 initial guide): -6.6%. 2025-10-21 (Q3 beat): +1.36%.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. FY consensus of about $22.96 already sits above the guide midpoint of $22.875. What is unpriced is only how far the range narrows, and the roughly 12% drawdown since the Q2 print suggests expectations for the multiple, not the estimates, have reset lower.
findings.independence: The Q1 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000102729/000110465926045698/vmi-20260421xex99d1.htm) and the Q2 call summary (https://www.marketbeat.com/earnings/reports/2026-7-21-valmont-industries-inc-stock/) are separate company documents. Both are company statements, not independent demand data.

outside_window.finding: Lindsay Corporation (irrigation peer) reports fiscal Q4 2026 (ended Aug 31) before the open on 2026-10-22, after VMI's window closes. Its fiscal Q3 showed international irrigation down 4% on lower Brazil volumes and irrigation operating income down 25%.
Arcosa (utility and engineered structures peer) Q3 2026 results are projected for 2026-10-29 or 2026-11-04, unconfirmed and after the window.

searched_and_found_nothing: Analyst actions after July 2026: none found. The latest are Stifel PT $678 (2026-07-20), JPMorgan $620 (2026-07-22) and the Zacks downgrade to Hold; Benzinga's consensus on 2026-09-14 was Neutral with a $583 target. The Benzinga ratings pages returned 403.
Cause of the ~12% slide since the Q2 print and the 4% fall in the last 5 sessions: no company-specific news, 8-K or sector sell-off story found for September or October 2026.

The only Form 4 read was a 310-share RSU grant to new CLO Toni Hickey (2026-09-08); the others since July (07-24 through 08-19, following a Form 144 on 07-27) were not opened. No new 8-K since July 28.
EDGAR full-text search for 'IEEPA' in VMI filings during 2026: zero hits, so no tariff-refund receivable is disclosed.
VMI conference commentary in September 2026 (e.g. D.A. Davidson): nothing found.
Utility steel-pole lead times or competitor capacity news for Q3 2026: nothing specific found.
US center-pivot dealer or farm-equipment demand data for fall 2026: only market-research boilerplate.
Peer prints before Oct 20 on utility structures (Arcosa) and irrigation (Lindsay): both report after the window.

baseline_tension: The evidence is balanced: it neither agrees nor disagrees with the mild +1.81 put skew and the 'balanced' lean. The soft run-up (-4.6% over 20 days, 23% below the high) means expectations for the multiple have reset, which slightly favours a beat being rewarded, but the Q2 beat and raise was sold, so this does not move p_up off 50.
lessons_applied: Lesson 9 (size a segment net of the rest): AZZ coatings read-through cut from +0.4 to +0.3, because coatings is under ~10% of VMI sales.

Lesson 6 (a finding inside what was already guided): HRC finding cut from -0.5 to -0.4, because management had already guided Q3 margin pressure from materials and only the increase after July 17 is new.
Lesson 5 (macro-to-company proxy): diesel finding cut from -0.4 to -0.3 and kept filed as a proxy.
Lesson 1 (a verified fact is not a predicted reaction; this name sold its Q2 beat and raise): beat-and-raise finding cut from +0.3 to +0.2, with p_up kept at 50.
Net: the sum is unchanged at -0.2 and the scaled number at 0; only the individual sizes moved.
